disease_label_per_paper: Salmonella typhimurium infection in total knee arthroplasty
presentation_summary: A 72-year-old woman presented 4 years after bilateral total knee arthroplasty with 5 months of severe right knee pain, swelling, and discharging sinus.
Exam showed swelling, tenderness, painful movements, severely limited range of motion, and sinus discharge from two sites.
WBC was 6.2 x10^9/L with 61.1% polymorphonuclear leukocytes, ESR 88 mm/h, and CRP 51.3 mg/L.
Right knee radiographs showed prosthesis loosening.
She underwent implant removal, debridement, frank pus drainage, and gentamicin cement spacer placement; cultures grew Salmonella Typhimurium.
